**Job Description**  

New York City Emergency Management (NYCEM) helps New Yorkers before, during, and after emergencies through preparedness, education, and response. NYCEM is responsible for coordinating citywide emergency planning and response for all types and scales of emergencies. We are staffed by more than 200 dedicated professionals with diverse backgrounds and areas of expertise, including individuals assigned from other City agencies.  

  

The Office of the Chief Counsel provides legal advice to NYCEM executives and staff regarding critical, strategic, legal and policy issues facing the agency, engages in transactional work in support of the NYCEM mission and coordinates with the NYC Law Department, Office of the Chief Counsel to the Mayor and City Hall, and other local, state and federal counsels regarding various legal issues ranging from emergency events to litigation, which impact the agency. The Office of Chief Counsel is comprised of the Legal Affairs Unit, the Civil and Human Rights Unit formerly known as the Disability, Access and Functional Needs Unit (DAFN), and the Records Management Unit.  

  

The Records Management Unit is responsible for leading and managing the NYCEM records management program. It develops and implements policies and procedures to manage agency records throughout their life cycle, from creation to their final disposition, and works with units and personnel to ensure all staff are aware of and can apply records management best practices into their daily course of business.  

  

The Office of the Chief Counsel is seeking a Deputy Director of Records who will oversee work of the Records Management unit and supervise the Records Program Manager and any temporary staff, including interns. The Deputy Director of Records will oversee the maintenance and management the agency’s electronic and physical records. This includes any day\-to\-day responsibilities and creating and implementing policies around agency records. The Deputy Director of Records will work with staff to ensure that all records are in compliance according to City policies and procedures.  

  

Under the supervision of the Chief Counsel, the Deputy Director of Records will have responsibilities including but not limited to the following:  

  

* Overseeing Records Management unit staff and interns.
* Managing and maintaining an electronic records management system, currently RecordPoint’s Records365\.
* Performing day\-to\-day records management tasks and activities relating to storage, retrieval, retention and disposition of records.
* Training staff in the procedures related to policies governing the maintenance of all documents (both records and non\-records, regardless of format) and ensuring staff are aware of their role in the management of agency records.
* Overseeing all Records Management unit functions and projects including but not limited to reviewing and updating the retention schedule as needed, applying retention to records in SharePoint using Records365, creating destruction and transfer requests, choosing a system to manage physical records (potentially Records365\).
* Developing and implementing agency records management policies and related procedures as needed and performing yearly reviews and updates of established policies.
* Creating one page infographics to communicate important policies or procedures to NYCEM staff as needed.
* Overseeing all scanning projects which must follow the NYC Department of Records and Information Services’ (DORIS) processes and guidelines and be approved by DORIS before projects may commence. Potential scanning projects include eligible agency records with long\-term retention periods or special scanning projects (e.g., activation records to be transferred to another City agency).
* Maintaining filing system procedures and classification indexes.
* Assigning and managing file space as well as inventorying boxes and preparing materials for storage or transfer to the NYC Municipal Records Center if needed.
* Working with staff to ensure all agency publications that are required to be submitted to the NYC Municipal Library are transferred to the Records Management unit for submission to the Library’s Government Publications Portal.
* Choosing, inventorying and cataloging materials in the agency library and managing patrons and the circulation of the collection utilizing ResourceMate Plus.
* Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex assignments, exercise sound judgment, and communicate progress to leadership.

Outside of activations, EOC members participate in periodic training and exercises to maintain operational readiness, and must volunteer to assist with three Ready NY emergency preparedness presentations per year. EOC teams are on call for three weeks at a time, with six weeks off in between.

### **Description**

  

The YMCA of Greater Boston is a leading partner of The Greater Boston Food Bank and operates a comprehensive hunger prevention network serving neighborhoods throughout Boston. Through its warehouse distribution center, the YMCA packages and delivers more than 4,500 grocery bags each week to over 45 community partner organizations. In addition, the YMCA operates two Mobile Market Food Trucks that serve more than 30 locations across the city, providing fresh, nutritious food through a client\-choice model that increases accessibility and dignity for participants. The YMCA also partners with Codman Square Health Center to support a Community Market in Dorchester serving more than 600 residents weekly. Collectively, these programs distribute more than 2\.5 million meals annually.

As leaseholder and manager of the Collaborative Food Access Hub, the YMCA works closely with partner organizations to strengthen food access throughout Greater Boston. The Director of Operations, Hunger Prevention Programs provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for all YMCA hunger prevention initiatives, including Mobile Markets, grocery bag distribution, warehouse operations, food procurement, inventory management, compliance, data reporting, volunteer engagement, and community partnerships. This position works closely with the Director of Operations for the Collaborative Food Access Hub to ensure seamless communication, coordination, and daily logistics among partner organizations and YMCA staff.### **Key Responsibilities**

  

**Operational Leadership \& Program Management*** Provide strategic and operational leadership for Mobile Markets, grocery bag distribution programs, warehouse operations, and community food access initiatives.
* Lead cross\-functional collaboration across YMCA departments, Collaborative Food Access Hub partners, and community stakeholders to drive operational excellence, strengthen service delivery, and achieve hunger prevention objectives.
* Oversee daily operations to ensure safe, efficient, equitable, and high\-quality service delivery.
* Coordinate Mobile Market schedules, routes, partner site calendars, and distribution logistics.
* Ensure operational readiness, business continuity, and emergency food response capabilities across all hunger prevention programs.
* Develop and implement process improvements that enhance efficiency, inventory accuracy, customer experience, and program impact.
* Establish and monitor operational goals, service standards, and key performance indicators (KPIs).
* Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to support the annual distribution of more than 2\.5 million meals.

**Administration \& Operations Management*** Support the Pantry Operations Manager in administering the Grocery Bag Distribution Program, including partner communications, scheduling, donation coordination, reporting, and procurement activities.
* Manage relationships with community partners and serve as a primary operational liaison.
* Coordinate monthly Mobile Market schedules and communications with partner sites and YMCA website staff.
* Serve as the lead administrator and subject matter expert for the Inventory Management System (IMS), ensuring inventory accuracy, data integrity, system utilization, reporting compliance, staff training, and continuous process improvement.
* Manage food procurement through The Greater Boston Food Bank, local farms, and other vendors.
* Review and maintain Bills of Lading (BOLs), inventory records, delivery documentation, and operational reports.
* Support warehouse operations, inventory control, logistics, and food distribution activities as needed.
* Maintain accurate operational records and documentation to support reporting, compliance, and audit requirements.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Executive Director.

**Staff Leadership \& Volunteer Engagement*** Supervise program staff, drivers, volunteers, interns, seasonal employees, and temporary personnel.
* Lead recruitment, hiring, onboarding, training, scheduling, coaching, and performance evaluations.

The American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) seeks a dynamic, growth\-oriented science policy leader to take the Center for Scientific Evidence in Public Issues (EPI Center) (https://www.aaas.org/programs/epi\-center) into its next phase.

**Description**


The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and 182 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org


**VPU Context:**The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) is a shared commitment to end the world’s learning crisis. It is the only global partnership and fund dedicated entirely to helping children in lower\-income countries get a quality education, so they can unlock their potential and contribute to building a better world.


We bring together governments, teachers, civil society, donors, United Nations agencies, development banks, businesses and private foundations to transform education systems so that every girl and boy can have hope, opportunity and agency.


**What We Do**


GPE helps low\- and lower\-middle\-income countries build stronger education systems so that all children can get the education they need to thrive. We support more than 90 countries where the needs are greatest and focus on reaching the children who are the most vulnerable, including girls, children with disabilities, and those affected by extreme poverty or conflict. Our unique approach works. Between 2021 and 2025, GPE supported 372 million children in partner countries to get a better education through grants and co\-financing.


**How We Work**


GPE is working to help governments transform their education systems to get the most vulnerable children in school, improve teaching and learning, and build equitable, inclusive and resilient education systems fit for the 21st century. Transforming education is about creating lasting changes and achieving impact on a scale. GPE sets out to deliver this transformative change by convening partners, mobilizing funds and catalyzing reforms to help partner countries accelerate access, learning outcomes and gender equality.


**Multiply Possibility – Financing GPE 2030**


GPE launched its 5th financing campaign for 2026\-2030, co\-hosted by Italy and Nigeria, to mobilize $5 billion for inclusive, high\-performing education systems in the world’s most challenging contexts. This funding will unlock $15 billion in total education investment through co\-financing and multiplier effects. A fully funded GPE will transform education systems and multiply possibility for 750 million children in 96 countries.


**Governance And Organizational Arrangements**


The GPE Board of Directors includes ministerial\-level board members and alternates representing 20 constituencies that reflect the partnership’s breadth. The Board Chair is H.E. President Jakaya Kikwete and the Board Vice Chair is Ms. Christine Hogan. The American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) seeks a dynamic, growth\-oriented science policy leader to take the Center for Scientific Evidence in Public Issues (EPI Center) (https://www.aaas.org/programs/epi\-center) into its next phase.


The EPI Center bolsters public decisions about the most important issues of our day by facilitating scientific evidence’s inclusion in a complex process through high\-touch, high\-context dialogue and resources.



The EPI Center advances evidence\-informed decision making by:


* Bringing policy\-relevant, unbiased, non\-partisan scientific evidence to public decisionmakers at all levels of government;
* Facilitating multi\-sector and multi\-stakeholder engagements (virtual and in\-person) to build trusted relationships between scientists and policymakers to deliver clear, actionable, and timely information to the people who need it most.


The Center's collaborative engagement model leverages partnerships with nationally recognized civic intermediaries—including the National Governors Association, the National League of Cities, the National Conference of State Legislatures, and the Council of State Governments—to reach state and local decision\-makers across the political spectrum. To date, EPI Center projects have reached over 10,000 decision\-makers, including officials in every state, U.S. territory, and Washington, DC, enabling policymakers to more easily access, understand and incorporate scientific expertise into their decision\-making.


*Help us ignite the next era of science.*

  


**What You’ll Do**



As the Center enters the next phase of its growth, the **Director of the EPI Center** has ultimate responsibility for setting the Center’s long\-term strategy and overseeing its day\-to\-day operations, leading a high\-performing team of professionals and an ever\-growing network of collaborators.
